candidates.exact_span: The known uses of the receiving water(s) Segment 20.6.4.98 are livestock watering, wildlife habitat, marginal warmwater aquatic life and primary contact.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Different interpretation of which designated/known uses apply to the receiving segment could change which water-quality-based numeric criteria (e.g., pH) are selected as the enforceable limit for compliance comparison.

candidates.exact_span: The known uses of Segment 20.6.4.99 are warmwater aquatic life, livestock watering, wildlife habitat, and primary contact.
candidates.computation_change_reason: If the discharge is attributed to Segment 20.6.4.99 rather than 20.6.4.98, the applicable use classifications—and thus which numeric WQS criteria govern—could differ, changing the selected discharge limit.

candidates.exact_span: The designated uses of Animas River, in both Section 20.6.4.403 and 404 NMAC, are coolwater aquatic life, irrigation, livestock watering, wildlife habitat, public water supply, industrial water supply and primary contact.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of whether Animas River designated uses (rather than segment 98/99 known uses) govern limit selection could change which pH and other WQS criteria are treated as the operative enforceable limits.

candidates.exact_span: The limiting pH numeric criteria in 20.6.4.900 NMAC for primary contact and warmwater, marginal warmwater and coolwater aquatic life designated uses are pH within the range of 6.6 to 9.0 standard units (su).
candidates.computation_change_reason: This passage states the numeric pH range that would be compared against reported measurements; a different reading of the cited criteria or use-to-criterion mapping would change the applicable limit and exceedance determination.

candidates.exact_span: The site-specific pH standard of 6.6 – 9.0 is established at the end-of-pipe.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether the enforceable pH limit is applied at end-of-pipe versus another location (e.g., in-stream) affects which monitoring results are eligible for numeric compliance comparison.

candidates.exact_span: The NMIP requires site-specific pH standard to be applied at end-of-pipe for all dischargers.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of NMIP applicability could determine whether end-of-pipe is the mandatory compliance point for pH, changing which reported values are compared to the numeric limit.

candidates.exact_span: The limitation and monitoring requirements for pH of 6.6 to 9 are continued in the draft permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether 'continued in the draft permit' establishes that the 6.6–9.0 pH limit and its associated monitoring obligations are operative for the permit term affects both which numeric limit applies (A) and whether pH monitoring was required (B).

candidates.exact_span: The facility is a minor industrial with the highest monthly average flow over the most recent 24-months as 0.177 MGD (0.274 cfs). For industrial facilities, the highest monthly average flow over the most recent 24-months is used for reasonable potential calculations.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The stated effluent flow figure and the rule for selecting it feed reasonable-potential modeling; a different interpretation of the flow value or calculation basis could change whether water-quality-based effluent limits for toxics are imposed.

candidates.exact_span: The facility discharges to an irrigation ditch. Water only flows in the ditch when the fields need water. The rest of the year the ditch is dry, 4Q3 is 0.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Intermittent discharge and 4Q3=0 affect reasonable-potential/receiving-water dilution inputs (A), whether monitoring is required only during discharge events or seasons (B), and whether documented dry periods constitute no-discharge or conditional non-monitoring states (C).

candidates.exact_span: No samples have been taken of the ditch water when flowing and there are no ambient data.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Absence of ambient and in-ditch flow samples bears on whether reasonable-potential analysis can support toxics effluent limits (A) and how missing or unavailable evidence for expected monitoring periods should be classified (C).
